description: We are the Meninas Cientistas (Girls in Science) project, coordinated by Professor Muriel de Pauli at the State University of Santa Catarina (UDESC), Brazil. Our mission is to encourage girls to explore science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), empowering them to become active participants in scientific discovery and innovation.
summary:
Space Mission – Destiny Is in Your Hands is an educational, interactive game for children aged 7 to 12 that puts players in the role of space mission commanders. Their goal is to plan and carry out a journey to the Moon or Mars, using reasoning, strategy, and decision-making to overcome each challenge. Through a fun and accessible adventure, the game introduces concepts of space exploration, engineering, science, and resource management, showing how every choice can affect the success of the mission.

The adventure starts with choosing a destination and receiving a budget of 5,000 coins, to be spent on essentials such as oxygen, water, food, thermal clothing, and medicine. Players then customize the rocket and the astronaut and prepare for launch by connecting electrical wires and refueling the spacecraft. During the six-day journey, they track resource consumption, monitor equipment, and handle unexpected events such as technical failures and meteor showers.

Upon arrival, players carry out scientific activities, collect samples, answer educational questions, and help repair an exploration robot. In the final stage, an emergency damages the spacecraft and players must find parts to repair it, then manage their resources again on the trip back to Earth.

Along the way, participants develop logical reasoning, planning, problem solving, creativity, and decision-making, while learning how real space missions work and why planning and teamwork matter.
details:
Space Mission – Destiny Is in Your Hands! is an educational, interactive game designed for children aged 7 to 12. Players act as commanders of a mission to the Moon or Mars. They choose a destination and receive a budget of 5,000 coins. They spend it on oxygen, water, food, thermal clothing, and medicine, then customize the rocket and the astronaut.

Before launch, they complete tasks such as connecting electrical wires and refueling the spacecraft. The six-day journey requires tracking supplies, monitoring equipment, and handling technical failures and meteor showers. Upon arrival, players collect samples, complete science challenges, answer educational questions, and help repair an exploration robot. In the final stage, an emergency damages the spacecraft, requiring players to find replacement parts, repair it, and manage their resources again on the journey back to Earth.

What benefits does it offer?

The game transforms space-mission planning into a fun, accessible learning experience. Children practice logical reasoning, planning, problem-solving, creativity, and decision-making. They also explore fundamental concepts in science, engineering, and technology, discovering how real space missions depend on careful preparation, scientific knowledge, and resource management.

What is the intended impact?

We aim to spark children's curiosity about science and space exploration. By making different choices and experiencing their consequences, players learn that a successful mission depends on planning, organization, knowledge, and teamwork, not only on advanced technology. The game also encourages an early interest in STEM fields (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics).

What tools, languages, hardware, or software were used?

The game was developed with the assistance of Claude, an artificial intelligence tool used to support the programming and development process. Scientific research and educational content were informed by resources from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), helping connect the game to real scientific data and space research.

The game is built as a single, self-contained web page using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, without external libraries. The scenes are rendered using the browser's Canvas technology, while the rocket and astronaut are created with vector (SVG) graphics.

It runs in a standard web browser on computers, tablets, and smartphones, supporting keyboard, mouse, and touchscreen controls. No special hardware or software installation is required.

What is the creative aspect?

  • Players are commanders rather than spectators, and every decision has visible consequences.
  • A limited budget forces players to make strategic trade-offs between essential supplies.
  • Players can personalize their own rocket and astronaut.
  • Mini-games, a walkable 360° spacecraft cabin, and surface exploration make the experience feel like a real space adventure.
  • Educational fact cards connect gameplay to real space science, including Apollo Moon samples, NASA's DONKI space-weather records, the Perseverance rover, and Olympus Mons.
  • The integration of AI-assisted development and NASA scientific resources combines accessible game design with authentic scientific references.

What factors did the team consider?

  • Age-appropriateness: Simple language, large buttons, and a friendly tone designed for children aged 7 to 12.
  • Balance of fun and learning: Every challenge incorporates a specific educational objective.
  • Accessibility: The game works across different screen sizes and input methods, includes a sound on/off button, and respects reduced-motion settings.
  • Realistic constraints: Limited resources, equipment failures, and emergencies reflect the real challenges of space missions.
  • Scientific accuracy: NASA-related scientific resources were considered to bring authentic space exploration concepts into the gameplay and encourage curiosity about real scientific discoveries.
